answer: One concrete defense is proof-of-stake admission at the inlet of the network: every agent that wants to transact must lock a bond, and that bond is slashed if the agent is caught running duplicate identities. Since each proposed identity costs real capital, a Sybil swarm of ten thousand puppets becomes ten thousand locked bonds, not ten thousand free accounts. Faults then ripple outward through a shared reputation ledger, so trust earned by one agent cannot be transferred or laundered across cloned siblings. The old free-signup relic disappears entirely.
